sections.title: Questions 21–26
sections.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Eyewitness reliability 21 Eleanor thinks eyewitnesses are believed when

sections.title: Questions 27–30
sections.instruction: What problem may there be with child witnesses at each of the following stages of an interview? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 27–30.

questions.question: Eleanor thinks eyewitnesses are believed when

options.label: A they are respected members of the community.
options.html: they are respected members of the community.

options.label: B they make their statements with confidence.
options.html: they make their statements with confidence.

options.label: C they use sophisticated language in their accounts.
options.html: they use sophisticated language in their accounts.

questions.question: What concerns Duckie Eleanor and Jamie about the texts they have read so far?

options.label: A No clear conclusions are reached
B The studies involved comparatively few people.
options.html: The studies involved comparatively few people.

options.label: C Some of the data were gathered some time ago.
options.html: Some of the data were gathered some time ago.

questions.question: They agree that the most significant factor affecting eyewitness reliability is

options.label: A how good the lighting is.
B how long the event lasts.
C how far away the witness is.
options.html: how far away the witness is.

questions.question: Jamie criticises photo-identifications, saying witnesses

options.label: A fail to compare the photos with their memory of the event.
options.html: fail to compare the photos with their memory of the event.

options.label: B are not properly briefed about the procedure.
options.html: are not properly briefed about the procedure.

options.label: C become easily influenced by a figure of authority.
options.html: become easily influenced by a figure of authority.

questions.question: They agree that the term ‘naive observer’ means a person who

options.label: A has no experience of a police investigation.
options.html: has no experience of a police investigation.

options.label: B did not realise they were witnessing a crime.
options.html: did not realise they were witnessing a crime.

options.label: C was not present at the incident.
options.html: was not present at the incident.

questions.question: They have learned that witnesses are reluctant to change their opinions because

options.label: A they do not want to appear foolish.
options.html: they do not want to appear foolish.

options.label: B they fear the legal consequences.
C they are keen for the case to be concluded.
options.html: they are keen for the case to be concluded.
